title: Main Page
wikitext:
Welcome to '''Bardic Torch''': a collaborative wiki dedicated to the music, stories, and performances of the bardic community.

This wiki is intended to help bards find music, lyrics, history, context, etiquette information, and information about other bards - and to help audience members find that song they loved around the campfire but forgot the title of! We aim to take the vast variety of online songbooks, playlists, lyric sheets and album pages and collect all the information in one place. We also aim to help conserve and preserve these works so they are not lost or forgotten.

This wiki is community-maintained. It is not officially associated with the SCA nor with any other re-enactment organization, LARP organization, fan convention, SF&F organization, filk group, musical group, or other thing that might be described as "official".

If you just want to go directly to the index of all works, go to [[:Category:Pieces|Pieces]]. If you want to search for pieces by category, [[:Category:Top_Level_Categories|Top Level Categories]] should contain everything.

'''If you are on mobile, we strongly recommend enabling "desktop mode". Several important features do not work on mobile!'''

----

= Categories =
See the [[Categories]] page for more information.

* [[:Category:Bards|Bards]]  
* [[:Category:Pieces|Pieces]]
** Pieces by genre: [[:Category:Songs|Songs]], [[:Category:Poems|Poems]], [[:Category:Stories|Stories]], [[:Category:Instrumental|Instrumental]], [[:Category:Dances|Dances]], [[:Category:Comedy|Comedy]]
** Pieces by mood: [[:Category:Tragic|Tragic]], [[:Category:Comedic|Comedic]], [[:Category:Joyful|Joyful]], [[:Category:Warlike|Warlike]], [[:Category:Relaxed|Relaxed]], [[:Category:Sentimental|Sentimental]], [[:Category:Dance Music|Dance Music]], [[:Category:Story (Mood)|Story (Mood)]], [[:Category:Romantic|Romantic]], [[:Category:Singalong|Singalong]], or see all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]].
** Pieces by topic: See [[:Category:Topics]]
** Pieces by culture: See [[:Category:Cultures]]
** Pieces by source category: [[:Category:Pre-1600 Sources|Pre-1600 Sources]], [[:Category:Traditional&Folk|Traditional & Folk]], [[:Category:Borrowings|Borrowings (Modern songs from outside the community)]], [[:Category:SCA Pieces|SCA Pieces]], [[:Category:SF&F Pieces|SF&F Pieces]],[[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta (new words to old music)]], [[:Category:Contrafacta (Modern)|Contrafacta (Modern) (adaptations and parodies of modern songs)]], [[:Category:Setting Pieces|Setting Pieces (new music to old words)]]
** For languages other than English, see [[:Category:Languages|Languages]]
** For particular mythos, see [[:Category:Legendaria|Legendaria]]
* [[Collections]]
* [[Conservation Status]]

----

= How to Contribute =

Because anyone can contribute to Bardic Torch, it’s easier for all of us to work together to make sure the information isn’t gone forever when links go dead, social media websites go down, or paper gets lost.  Please make an account if you wish to contribute. Anyone is welcome and encouraged to help us collate and record the vast quantity of information available. 

Please be careful not to upload large files to the wiki or place copyrighted content on the wiki. In the vast majority of cases, the wiki should link to lyrics and recordings elsewhere. If the lyrics of a song are public domain or licenced under Creative Commons, it is acceptable to write the lyrics into the song’s wiki page. Do not attempt to host audio or video directly here. Do not upload private information about bards; stick to what is available on their publicly-facing websites. 

See [[Get Started Contributing]] for more help.

----

= For Bards =

You should feel free (but not obliged) to create and edit your own page! Anyone qualifies for a page if there is enough content - see [[:Category:Bards|Bards]]. 

It is extremely important that bards’ and authors’ preferences are not only respected by Bardic Torch, but actively broadcast by it. We aim to make it easier to find out information about licensing and etiquette - from who wrote a song, to whether a song is public domain or Creative Commons or you should ask the author for permission, to whether the author prefers to be contacted about performances of their songs, to how authors feel about lyric edits or sing-alongs or spinoff content.

Please ensure all such information has a source link: do not edit the wiki to say that you wrote a song, or that you give permission for its performance, or that you prefer to be informed about new performance uploads. Write that information on your own blog, website or album page - then link to it from here. You can really help us by creating a centralised page that lets bards know how they can interact with your work; see the [[Bard Preference Checklist]] for help creating one!

Similarly, we'd love to make sure your preferences are respected if you want any information about you to be taken down or changed or hidden. If you contact us and ask us to take a page down, there's a risk that somebody else might put the page back up in the future. Please write something on your own blog or website stating your preferences clearly (eg. "I do not wish wiki pages to be created about me", "I do not wish recordings of my performances to be placed online" or "I do not wish my song lyrics to be shared anywhere except my personal page") so that we can cite that source on the wiki. We can then add that note to your bardic page, with a citation, so that every future editor knows not to share or publish the information - and everyone who reads the wiki will know not to upload that information either, elsewhere.

(If you contact us and ask us to take a page down, we will of course do our best! And nobody should upload copyrighted information to our wiki - only link to where it is hosted elsewhere. We will never host recordings of your songs here directly.)

See also [[FAQ for Bards]].

----

= Why Bardic Torch? =

Why create a new wiki, when so many online indexes and archives already exist? Why not contribute to expanding existing lists? 

Bardic Torch doesn't aim to replace existing archives. Fantastic online resources exist - see [[Collections]]. Instead we aim to make the existing resources ''findable''. Miraheze's MediaWiki software enables us to put every bard page and every song/story/poem page into numerous categories, so you can search for pieces by mood or topic or century or kingdom - and if there's another criterion you'd like to be able to search by, you can create an account and begin categorising pieces that way. (See [[Categories]].)

We can also add links to where different versions of lyrics or different performances are hosted, all across the Web. We ''do not directly host works''. Many bardic works have been lost to history because the only version available was on a website that went down, or in a physical book that has been lost. We hope that when you find an [[:Category:Endangered|Endangered]] or [[:Category:Critically Endangered|Critically Endangered]] work on Bardic Torch, you will be encouraged to find it and add it to one of those other collections! 

Finally, ''anyone can edit this wiki''. Any archive maintained by a single author, single kingdom or small group of people is limited by the amount of work that those people are able to find and put in - and at risk if those creators decide to stop maintaining it. Bardic Torch is for the ''entire'' community and can be edited by ''anyone'' - just make an account.

These three factors are related; archives that host works directly usually can't allow just anyone to edit them, because there's too high a risk of copyright violations. Indexes without extensive sub-category systems need to limit their scope so that anyone can find anything. Songbooks for use around a campfire must curate their song lists to keep the book's length reasonable to print and read from. Bardic Torch cannot replace any of those things. All are vital parts of an ecosystem to keep works preserved and available, make them findable by songbook-compilers and index-makers, and allow people to perform them together.

----

''Bardic Torch is a living project. Every contribution helps preserve and share the bardic tradition with visitors. Thank you to all editors!''

''The name "Bardic Torch" is inspired by two meanings: using a torch as a light to search by, and "passing the torch" by preserving works for the next generation.''

title: Categories
wikitext:
= Categories & Tagging Guide =

This wiki uses categories to organize songs, singers, stories, storytellers, poems, poets, fools, dances, bands, choirs, troupes, and all other sorts of bardic material. 
Please follow these guidelines to keep everything consistent and searchable.

See [[:Category:Top_Level_Categories]] for the full auto-updating list of top level categories.

----

== Categories for Pieces ==

All pieces should belong to [[:Category:Pieces|Pieces]]. 

Each song page has an infobox.
* "Lyrics by:" should link to the lyricist's page, and the piece should be added to their page. 
* "Tune by:" should link to the composer's page, and the piece should be added to their page. 
* The '''Genre''' category should always include Songs. It may also include Instrumental. 
* Choose one or more '''Mood''' categories
* Choose one or more '''Topic''' categories 
* Choose one or more '''Culture''' categories 
* There should generally be only one '''Source Category'''
* You may add additional categories under '''Other categories'''

Each poem page has an infobox. 
* "Author:" should link to the author's page, and the piece should be added to their page. 
* The '''Genre''' category should always be Poems.
* Choose one or more '''Mood''' categories
* Choose one or more '''Topic''' categories 
* Choose one or more '''Culture''' categories 
* There should generally be only one '''Form''' category
* There should generally be only one '''Source Category'''
* You may add additional categories under '''Other categories'''

The infoboxes for stories and other genres are not set up yet.

Each documentable historical piece should also have a special infobox. 
* '''Source''' should link to the source. 
* '''Century'''

Categories are added automatically (or manually) at the bottom of pages.

----

=== Genre ===
Choose '''one''':

* [[:Category:Songs|Songs]] should be used for all musical pieces that have lyrics that can be sung.
* [[:Category:Instrumental|Instrumental]] should be used for all musical pieces that have sheet music available for instrumentalists. A musical piece be tagged as both 'Songs' and 'Instrumental' if it can be performed by both singers and instrumentalists. 
* [[:Category:Stories|Stories]] should be used for all narrative spoken pieces, regardless of format or tradition or length.
* [[:Category:Poems|Poems]] should be used for all poems that are '''not''' set to music. Epic poems may be categorised as both stories and poems. Please do not tag songs as poems, even if the lyrics rhyme. 
* [[:Category:Dances|Dances]] should be used for dance performances.
* [[:Category:Comedy|Comedy]] should be used for performances that fall under fooling and foolery, standup comedy, jester acts, clowning or similar work. 

Additional genres may be added later for work that truly cannot be categorised under the existing scheme, but please keep the number of tags limited. 

----

=== Mood ===
The wiki uses a '''limited''' number of mood tags to help ensure work is findable and the tag system remains manageable. The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag.

* [[:Category:Tragic|Tragic]] should be used for all pieces that are sad, mournful, tragic, wistful, solemn, or otherwise suitable for more sombre occasions; sad song contests, funerals, etc.
* [[:Category:Comedic|Comedic]] should be used for all pieces that are funny, silly, comic or humorous; suitable for parties and taverns, unsuitable for sombre occasions. 
* [[:Category:Joyful|Joyful]] should be used for all pieces that are happy, victorious, triumphant, upbeat, 'party' music or otherwise suitable for celebrations. 
* [[:Category:Warlike|Warlike]] should be used for pieces that are suitable for performance on a re-enactment battlefield or in relation to martial arts activities; often these will be war-related, angry, determined, fierce or upbeat.
* [[:Category:Relaxed|Relaxed]] should be used for pieces that are calm, lullabies, sweet, soft, soothing and otherwise suitable for a late-night quiet campfire or for sleepy audiences. 
* [[:Category:Sentimental|Sentimental]] should be used for pieces that are highly emotional, but don't fit into the strictly-happy Joyful or strictly-sad Tragic categories; those that are wistful, nostalgic, sweet, inspiring, uplifting, persuasive, longing or philosophical.
* [[:Category:Dance Music|Dance Music]] should be used for musical pieces that a bard may wish to perform at a dance, for dancers. They can be happy or sad, but should be pieces that a dance has been performed to. Distinct from [[:Category:Dances|Dances]], which is for the dances themselves. 
* [[:Category:Story Mood|Story (Mood)]] should be used when a piece tells a story too complex to categorise as happy or sad, because both kinds of events happen. It should be used for pieces that have a distinct plot arc.
* [[:Category:Romantic|Romantic]] should be used for music that is romantic; it may be suitable for weddings, or for performing to a romantic interest as part of flirting, or it may include praise pieces about the performer's partner/spouse/inspiration.
* [[:Category:Singalong|Singalong]] should be used for songs that are often used as group singalong songs. They typically have very easy melodies, upbeat tempo, simple well-known lyrics, actions and/or call-and-response sections.
* [[:Category:Eerie|Eerie]] should be used for songs that are scary, eerie, creepy, sinister, ghostly, chilling, fear-inducing or unsettling; suitable for Halloween celebrations, spooky song contests, or to perform alongside ghost stories.
* [[:Category:Rude|Rude]] - Use for works that contain bawdy, profane or blasphemous content that might be inappropriate to perform in front of children or polite company.

Try to use one of these broad categories as a piece's mood in its infobox. It is possible to create more specific categories, which should be listed at [[:Category:Moods|Moods]], but remember that the 'mood' tag is intended to help bards find pieces ''appropriate for a particular context or situation''. We do not intend to split the 'Joyful' tag into 'Excited', 'Happy', 'Cheerful' or other extremely subjective sub-categories. You might, however, create a new category under 'Warlike' for songs suitable as marching songs, or a new category under 'Tragic' for songs specifically suitable at funerals/rememberances, or a new category under 'Romantic' for songs appropriate at weddings.

----

=== Topic ===
You can choose multiple topics from [[:Category:Topics|Topics]]. Choose only the main topics of the song, not every item mentioned in the song. 

Keep topics in the infobox broad — avoid overly specific tags. If it can be filed under an existing tag, use the existing tag. Create a new tag only if the topic cannot be reasonably filed under existing tags.

Use sub-categories for more specific topics wherever possible. For example, 'Swords', 'Battles' or 'Shieldwalls' should all be sub-categories of 'War' and not main topic headings. 

When you create a new topic, ensure you write <nowiki>[[Category:Topics]]</nowiki> in the topic's category page. This will ensure the topic is added to the list of [[:Category:Topics|Topics]]. When you create a new sub-category, add <nowiki>[[Category:X]]</nowiki> to the category's page, replacing "X" with the category it is a sub-category of; this will add it as a sub-category to the category's page.

----

=== Culture ===
Use broad cultural categories where possible.

The intent of Culture categories is not to categorise the bards' backgrounds, the language of pieces, or necessarily to correctly identify the origin culture of the piece. It is to help performers and audiences identify suitable repertoire for the persona or setting they are portraying in re-enactment or LARP - for example, to help someone with a Viking SCA persona find suitable pieces for Norse-themed performance, or to help someone find appropriate French or France-related pieces to perform at a LARP set in Paris.

Multiple Culture tags may apply to a piece. Culture tags can be applied based on the documentable origin of a work, the style of instrumentation or melody, mentions of cultural elements (eg. song lyrics about gods from a particular pantheon) or historical events, or literal description of a culture or place in the work's text.

When listing multiple broader and narrower Culture tags, move from broad to specific - eg. "European, British, English"

When you create a new culture category, make sure to tag the category page with the [[:Category:Cultures|Cultures]] category so that it shows up in the list of cultures.

----

=== Form ===
Form is the section of the Poem infobox to specify the form of the poem. Poetic forms are sets of rules regarding syllables per line, rhyme schemes, language use and other aspects of poetry. Examples might include:
* [[:Category:Sonnet|Sonnet]]
* [[:Category:Haiku|Haiku]]
* [[:Category:Muwashshah|Muwashshah]]
* [[:Category:Epic Poem|Epic Poem]]

Make sure to add new form categories to [[:Category:Forms|Forms]]. 

See also: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Poetic_forms Poetic Forms on Wikipedia]

----

=== Source Category ===
Bardic pieces come from many places; historically documentable pieces, original pieces written by members of modern bardic communities (including the SCA, LARP, SF&F, historical re-enactment and more), folk music, music from historical and fantasy fiction, filk, and more. The 'source category' field attempts to categorise works by their broad origin, whether someone dug them up from a twelfth-century manuscript or composed them at a Lord of the Rings convention.

'''Important:''' Please do not use "filk". The term "filk" has many different meanings in different communities; some commonly use it to refer to SF&F songs, while others use it exclusively for contrafacta and others use it for all 'nerd music'. We have created specific tags with clearer, agreed-upon meanings.

Choose '''one''':

* [[:Category:Pre-1600 Sources|Pre-1600 Sources]]  for pieces that are '''documentably''' pre-1600 in origin.
* [[:Category:Traditional & Folk|Traditional & Folk]] for pieces that are not documentably pre-1600, but are old enough to not be copyrightable (or do not have a known author). Do not use for pieces protected by copyright, even if they are in the folk 'genre'. 
* [[:Category:Borrowings|Borrowings]] for pieces created by modern authors who are '''not''' part of the bardic tradition, such as modern mundane bands, which may be often performed in a bardic context. Be especially careful of copyright with these pieces. 
* [[:Category:SCA Pieces|SCA Pieces]] for pieces written by bards performing in an SCA context. Do not use for any and all pieces performed in the SCA - only those written by members of the SCA.
* [[:Category:SF&F Pieces|SF&F Pieces]] for pieces relating to SF&F shows, books, movies, and other fandom. 
* [[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta]] for pieces that set new words to an existing, historical tune - also called "parody", "filk", "lyrical adaptation", "rewrite" and so on. Use 'contrafacta' in the infobox, but you may also categorise these pieces as pre-1600 (for documentably pre-1600 melodies) or traditional (for folk tunes), and may categorise them as SCA or SF&F if the new words were written by SCA or SF&F-related artists. If the piece sets new words to an existing modern tune that is under copyright, use [[:Category:Contrafacta (Modern)|Contrafacta (Modern)]] instead. If the piece sets new words to a tune written by an SCA bard, use [[:Category:Contrafacta (SCA)|Contrafacta (SCA)]] instead.
* [[:Category:Setting Pieces|Setting Pieces]] for pieces that set old words to a new tune - taking a historical poem or text and creating a new original melody for it. Use 'Setting Pieces' in the infobox, but you may also categorise these pieces as pre-1600 or traditional if the words are pre-1600 or traditional, and may categorise them as SCA or as Borrowings if the melody is by a contemporary composer. 

In the infobox for a piece, use '''only''' the categories from the list above; all pieces should be categorised as one of the above. If you wish to create other categories or source categories on this theme, please place them in the 'other categories' section of the work's infobox and add the category pages to [[:Category:Source Category|Source Category]]. 

----

=== Other Categories ===
Optional tags for special cases:

* [[:Category:True Events|True Events]] - Use for pieces that describe events that really happened (or are claimed to have really happened) within bardic or associated communities (eg. the SCA, re-enactment groups, LARP groups). Do not use for historical events!
* [[:Category:Long Pieces|Long Pieces]] - Use for pieces that exceed the limit of what can normally be performed at a bardic circle - 5+ minutes for songs, 10+ minutes for stories or epic poetry. 
* [[:Category:Short Pieces|Short Pieces]] - use for pieces that are unusually short (eg. one-minute stories, one-verse songs or one-stanza poems). 
* See [[:Category:Languages|Languages]] for languages other than English. 
* See [[:Category:Legendaria|Legendaria]] for pieces relevant to particular literary collections of legends and myths - eg. Arthuriana, the Fenian/Ossianic Cycle, Saints' lives. 

----

== Categories for Bards ==

All bards should belong to [[:Category:Bards|Bards]].

Bard pages are titled according to the name the bard presents themselves with online. Use the name they publish under as the URL name - whether this be a legal name, SCA name, stage name, or nickname - and then add other names in brackets to the page title. 

----

=== Affiliations ===

List affiliations from broad to specific, eg. "SCA - Kingdom Name - Household Name" 

* [[:Category:SCA Bards|SCA Bards]]
* [[:Category:Amtgard|Amtgard]]

----

=== Performer Categories ===

* [[:Category:Musicians|Musicians]]
** [[:Category:Singers|Singers]]
** [[:Category:Instrumentalists|Instrumentalists]]
** [[:Category:Songwriters|Songwriters]]
* [[:Category:Storytellers|Storytellers]]
* [[:Category:Jesters|Jesters]] - use for comics, fools, jokers, etc
* [[:Category:Poets|Poets]]
* [[:Category:Dancers|Dancers]]

title: Category:Bards
wikitext:
Bards includes all performers. See specific sub-categories for: 

* [[:Category:Musicians|Musicians]] - tag bards as Musicians if their page can cite at least three recordings of musical performance and/or original musical works.
** [[:Category:Singers|Singers]] - tag bards as Singers if their page can cite at least three recordings of their singing.
** [[:Category:Instrumentalists|Instrumentalists]] - tag bards as Instrumentalists if their page can cite at least three recordings of playing instruments. 
** [[:Category:Songwriters|Songwriters]] - tag bards as Songwriters if their page can cite at least three songs they have written.
* [[:Category:Storytellers|Storytellers]] - tag bards as Storytellers if their page can cite at least three recordings of storytelling performance and/or original stories.
* [[:Category:Jesters|Jesters]] - use for comics, fools, jokers, etc; tag bards as Jesters if their page can cite at least three comedic performances.
* [[:Category:Poets|Poets]] - tag bards as Poets if their page can cite at least three recordings of poetic performance and/or original poems.
* [[:Category:Dancers|Dancers]] - tag bards as Dancers if their page can cite at least three dance performance recordings and/or dance instruction articles.

It is acceptable (and encouraged) to create a page that does not ''yet'' contain three citations, and allow others to add more citations later. If you find a page that does not contain three citations, first try searching the web to see if additional citations can be added to the page. Only de-list a page from a category if it seems that three citations do not exist. '''All citations must be hosted elsewhere''' and linked to here.

title: Category:SCA Pieces
wikitext:
Bardic Torch uses a set number of 'Source Categories' to categorise the origins of pieces. Please use 'SCA Pieces' for pieces entirely written by bards performing in an SCA context.

Do not use for any and all pieces performed in the SCA - only those entirely written by members of the SCA for performance in the SCA. 

* Songs found in historical sources pre-1600 should be categorised as [[:Category:Pre-1600 Sources|Pre-1600 Sources]]. 
* Songs sung in the SCA, but which originate as traditional (out-of-copyright or unknown-author) folk tunes, should be categorised as [[:Category:Traditional Folk Music|Traditional/Folk Music]]. 
* Songs created by modern authors who are '''not''' part of the bardic tradition should be categorised as [[:Category:Borrowings|Borrowings]]. Be especially careful of copyright with these pieces. 
* If a bard is associated with the SCA, but the piece was written for SF&F spaces such as fan conventions, use [[:Category:SF and F Pieces|SF&F Pieces]].
* If an SCA bard sets new words to a historical tune, use [[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta]].
* If an SCA bard sets historical words to a new tune, use [[:Category:SettingPieces|Setting Pieces]]. 
For more information, see [[Categories]].

== Licensing & Etiquette ==
Please contribute to this page if you have (sourced) information. 
* [https://www.Legal Name.com/period-filk/ According to an essay on Legal Name 053, Lisa Theriot's opinions on the ethics of 'filking' (borrowing existing tunes for songs with new words)]: 
** "If the only way you’ll write songs is to use a tune from elsewhere, then by all means go ahead, but remember that the broadside sellers didn’t have the owners of the original tunes coming after them with lawyers.  Find a period dance tune or some other period song, or at the very least a song no longer under active copyright defense."
** "If I can tell by the lyrics alone what song you filked, it’s a definite problem in the creativity department and a potential problem of legality."
** "Someone once told me that they didn’t think a song of mine was long enough, so she offered to write a few more verses; none of her ideas had the slightest reference to the main storyline.  I declined.  But she did the right thing and asked first."
** "Some SCA writers have a “Fly, be free!” attitude about their work.  Others don’t.  Be a gracious and honorable gentle and Ask First."
** "Understand this: YOU NEED NOT SELL COPIES FOR MONEY to be in copyright violation. Putting your lyrics up on a web page or printing lyrics constitutes both publication and copyright infringement."

title: Atlantian Bloodsong
wikitext:
= Atlantian Bloodsong =
The Atlantian Bloodsong was written some time shortly after Atlantia became a kingdom. According to legend, Atlantia was in danger of losing kingdom status (becoming part of the East Kingdom again) because of a lack of signed-up SCA members. Rhiannon wrote this song and sang it across the kingdom - even singing it in East Kingdom court - to persuade people to sign up for memberships. She succeeded, and Atlantia never lost its independence.

== Lyrics ==
There are two versions of Belt and Chain; the Atlantian version and the original version. The Atlantian version was created when the song was brought to Atlantia, before the days of easily-accessible internet recordings, and the lyrics were either misremembered or deliberately changed. [http://merryrose.atlantia.sca.org/archive/1997-06jun/msg00428.html The author believed "simple 'data corruption' is more the culprit".]

* [https://Legal Name.atlantia.sca.org/A&S%20Files/Bardic/Belt%20and%20Chain%20-%20Atlantian.pdf Both versions of the lyrics in the Legal Name 025 songbook]
* [http://merryrose.atlantia.sca.org/archive/1997-06jun/msg00198.html Author's lyrics, as posted to the Merry Rose mailing list]
* [http://lists.ansteorra.org/pipermail/ansteorra-ansteorra.org/1997-June/008055.html Author's lyrics, as posted to the Ansteorran mailing list]

== Licensing & Etiquette ==
[http://merryrose.atlantia.sca.org/archive/1997-06jun/msg00428.html Morric Haast on the Merry Rose:]

"I would hope the Society as a culture continues to honor their bards and respect their works, not to mention adherence to the Berne Convention on copyrights, at least for
their own.

Case in point, though I've written my share of filk songs, I hold to two
measures of respect:  I have never filked a Society member's work without
permission (taboo in Trimaris), and I have never demeaned a song known to
bring tears or treasured by others (The Great Silky, for example) by using
its melody for another set of lyrics, humorous or not.  (Personally, I
only "filk" for humorous songs, but that's just me.)  OTOH, if _Pox on
You_(period) or _Mack the Knife_(duh) brings a tear to your eye, you'd
better let me know.

Both of these were entirely period practices, as were plagiarism and
trademark counterfeiting.  Still, I think the New Middle Ages should set
them aside, just as we have done with bear-baiting and religious
persecution.  As is evidenced by the Orders of the Pelican and Laurel, our
officers and artisans merit the same respect given to period aristocracy."

title: Category:Sentimental
wikitext:
The wiki uses a limited number of mood tags to help ensure work is findable and the tag system remains manageable. The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag. 

Sentimental should be used for pieces that are highly emotional, but don't fit into the strictly-happy Joyful or strictly-sad Tragic categories; those that are wistful, nostalgic, sweet, inspiring, uplifting, persuasive, longing or philosophical.

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].

title: Category:Traditional & Folk
wikitext:
Source categories on BardicTorch help to keep track of which works come from historically documentable sources, which were written by members of SCA / re-enactment / LARP communities, which originated in SF&F, which came from folk music, and so on. Please see [[Categories]] for more information. 

Use "Traditional & Folk" for pieces that are not documentably pre-1600, but are old enough to not be copyrightable (or do not have a known author). Do not use for pieces protected by copyright, even if they are in the folk 'genre'; use [[:Category:Borrowings|Borrowings]] for pieces by modern professional folk artists outside the bardic community.

== Licensing & Etiquette ==
[https://heatherdale.com/faq/#sing Heather Dale has a section of her FAQ that deals with licensing, permissions and etiquette.]
She states: 
* Bards have permission to sing her songs at events, so long as they give attribution. Heather also requests that people contact her to let her know how her music is being used. 
* Bards can contact her for permission to record a Heather Dale song on their own albums. 
* It is okay to make videos of her songs, so long as it's not-for-profit, gives attribution, and does not include objectionable content (porn, hatred, neo-Nazi, etc). 
* It is okay to rip her music from CDs to mp3 to listen on other devices, or lend CDs to friends, but not okay to re-upload her music to torrenting websites. 
* It is okay to write filk of her songs, with attribution. Send her an email with the filk. 
* Attribution should be given to heatherdale.com and the composer of the piece (likely Heather Dale, or Heather Dale & Legal Name 039)
Check her FAQ for more details.

title: Category:Topics
wikitext:
See [[Categories]] for more information about how topic tags should be used.

Use broad topics in the 'topic' section of a piece's infobox. Create subcategories wherever possible for more specific topics. For example:
* 'Swords', 'Fighting', 'Shieldwalls' or 'Battles' should all be subcategories of 'War' - not top-level categories.
* Topics such as 'Plants', 'Animals', 'Wildlife' or 'Forests' should be subcategories of 'Nature'.
* Topics such as 'Travel', 'Wanderlust', 'Exploration' or 'Sailing' should be subcategories of 'Wandering'.
* Topics such as 'Magic', 'Elves' or 'Mythical Creatures' should be subcategories of 'Supernatural'
* Topics such as 'Honour', 'Chivalry' or 'Praise Songs' should be subcategories of 'Virtues'

Notes on how to use topics:
* [[:Category:Patriotic|Patriotic]] - Use subcategories in brackets for the particular nation, kingdom or group being celebrated, eg. [[:Category:Patriotic (Atlantia)|Patriotic (Atlantia)]]
* [[:Category:Bardic Meta|Bardic Meta]] - use for songs about singing, stories about storytellers or poems about poetry 
* [[:Category:SCA (Topic)|SCA (Topic)]] - use for songs about the SCA - including its peerages, history, events, community, regalia, etc.
* [[:Category:Identity|Identity]] - use for songs about diversity, inclusion, belonging and pride for marginalised identities. 
* [[:Category:Historical People & Events|Historical People & Events]] - use for songs written about historical events and people 'by modern authors' - particularly songs aiming to educate about history.

When you create a new topic, ensure you add the [[:Category:Topics|Topics]] category to the category page. This will ensure the topic is added to the list of topics.

title: Get Started Contributing
wikitext:
The goal of Bardic Torch is to make it as easy as possible for anyone to contribute information - so that instead of thousands of songbooks/indexes/playlists/resources scattered across the internet, we can create one comprehensive wiki for the bardic community. 

Please make an account if you have anything to contribute. You do not have to be a bard. 

Feel free to [https://forms.gle/wUwWnMKtWZSUisWCA contact us] if you have a problem.

'''Easy Start Guide:''' There is now a step-by-step guide to adding a song at [[Easy Start Add a Song]]. 

== Guidelines for contribution ==

1. '''Any contribution, no matter how small, is appreciated.'''

In general, it's completely fine if your contribution is minimal. You can create a page for a bard even if you only know one song of theirs, or create a page for a song even if you don't know the lyrics. Somebody else can help by adding more information later. The most important thing is that you correctly link and categorise the pages, so that other people can find your work later and build upon it. Make sure you add as many category pages as should apply at the bottom of the page. Linking the category does not automatically put the page into the category. 

It can become difficult to find information in the bardic community when websites go offline, resources disappear or get taken down, and links go dead. Some pieces are probably lost forever because the paper is lost in somebody's attic and the MySpace or LiveJournal page went down. Our philosophy is therefore to have as many links as possible. Even if there are already four websites hosting the lyrics of a piece, it's still a useful contribution to add a fifth or sixth link. Even if we already have links to performances on Spotify or YouTube, it's still helpful to add links to performances on Bandcamp or SoundCloud. You never know when a website may go down. 

2. '''Do not upload private or personal information to Bardic Torch.'''

Stick to what bards have published on album pages, blogs and websites - do not cite private/personal social media posts. A public-facing social media page under a public name is ok, but no posts from private groups.

3. '''Do not upload copyrighted information.'''

Please do not upload copyrighted information to Bardic Torch. Link to performances and lyrics elsewhere - do not host them here. 

Lyrics can be hosted here if the song is released through Creative Commons or the public domain, but do not upload large files (images, videos) to the wiki. If you post lyrics to Bardic Torch, you must have a citation for the page where the bard stated that it was ok for anyone to reproduce and share the lyrics. There is not an exception if you are the author; please post permission elsewhere, then link to that permission as a citation. We cannot verify that you are the author from your Bardic Torch account.

4. '''Provide citations for information about licensing and etiquette.'''

We cannot verify who edited a Bardic Torch page, so you can't edit a page to say "I'm the author and I give permission for you to sing this song". You need to post that information from your own social media account, or on your own page or blog or website. Then you can link to that citation. 

If we allow "I heard third-hand around the campfire that this bard gives everyone permission to sell her music", there is an unacceptably high risk of our wiki encouraging and enabling copyright violations. Please encourage bards to talk about their preferences, licensing and permissions online.


== I need help understanding how to contribute ==
Bardic Torch is hosted on Miraheze, which uses [[w:MediaWiki]], the same software as Wikipedia. Once you make an account, you should be able to hit 'edit' on most pages and edit them in simple plaintext with markup. 

If you want to create a new page, you can simply visit the URL for the page you'd like to create; you should be prompted to create it.

If you have any issues creating a page, please try the following steps:
* Verify your email address. You may need to check your spam folder.
* Try editing a page first. Miraheze sometimes blocks accounts which it thinks are spammers.
* Miraheze sometimes blocks new users from adding external links. Try creating the page without any external links (you can use a blank template), then editing to add them in. 
* If none of this works, contact the administrator. 

=== Formatting ===

Use equals signs for titles. More equals will create a lower-level title. <nowiki>= Heading = will create a heading, while == Subheading == will create a subheading, and === Subheading === will create a sub-sub-heading.</nowiki>

Use asterisks for bullet points. More asterisks will create a more indented bullet. 
<syntaxhighlight lang="wikitext">* List item
* List item
** Sublist item
** Sublist item
* List item
</syntaxhighlight>

If you wish to link to an internal page, you only need to write its title in double square brackets. Be careful to get the name of the page exactly right. For example, <nowiki>[[Rosalind Jehanne]]</nowiki> will create a clickable link to our page on [[Rosalind Jehanne]], but <nowiki>[[Rosalin Jehann]]</nowiki> will fail. If you try to link to <nowiki>[[Pieces]], that won't work because the correct page is at</nowiki> [[:Category:Pieces]]. If you're not sure whether you've gotten things right, you can use "Show Preview" to check before saving your changes.

To link to an external page, simply use a single square bracket, and write the clickable text after the URL. For example, <nowiki>[www.google.com Click here to go to Google]</nowiki> will look like [https://www.google.com Click here to go to Google].

=== How to use Categories ===

'''TL;DR''': To make a clickable link to a category, use <nowiki>[[:Category:CategoryName|ClickableTextHere]]</nowiki>. [[:Category:Bards|Here is a clickable link to the Bards category.]] Doing this only creates a clickable link - it does not actually place the page inside the category. To place a page in a category, add <nowiki>[[Category:CategoryNameHere]]</nowiki> at the bottom of the page. To create subcategories, add <nowiki>[[Category:Sur-category]]</nowiki> to the category page of the subcategory.

'''Longer explanation''':

MediaWiki Miraheze ''automatically'' does lots of work to help us categorise songs. If you tag a page with a category, it will ''automatically'' be listed in that category's page - no extra work needed. For example, if you write <nowiki>[[Category:Comedic]]</nowiki> at the bottom of a song's page, it will not only add [[:Category:Comedic|Comedic]] to the categories infobox at the bottom of the song's page, it will ''automatically'' show up in the list when someone visits the [[:Category:Comedic|Comedic]] page.

''Linking to'' categories needs to be done differently to ''tagging a page with a category''.

When you write <nowiki>[[:Category:Comedic|Comedic]]</nowiki>, you create a clickable link - like the one in the paragraph above. It will not add this page to the 'Comedic' category, which is good - this page is an information page about how to contribute to the wiki, and doesn't belong in the category for funny songs and humorous stories. 

If you ''do not'' want to add a page to a category, use a : before you write Category: <nowiki>[[:Category:TextGoesHere]]</nowiki>. Then use | and write ''how you want the hyperlink to show up''. If you just write <nowiki>[[:Category:Comedic]]</nowiki>, it will look like [[:Category:Comedic]]. If you write <nowiki>[[:Category:Comedic|Click here to see the Comedic mood category!]]</nowiki>, it will look like [[:Category:Comedic|Click here to see the Comedic mood category!]]. 

If you ''do'' want to add a page to a category, don't use the : before you write Category: <nowiki>[[Category:TextGoesHere]]</nowiki>. This will automatically add the category to the page ''and'' automatically add the page to the category's index. However, when you do this, the text ''won't'' show up as a hyperlink - so this isn't the right format to use in a song's infobox. 

In many cases, you will want to ''both'' link to a category ''and'' tag a page with a category. A comedic song should have <nowiki>[[:Category:Comedic|Comedic]]</nowiki> in its infobox so that readers can click the link and see other comedic songs - ''and'' it should have <nowiki>[[Category:Comedic]]</nowiki> at the bottom of its page, so that it is categorised correctly. ''You need to do both.''

It is important that you get category names exactly right - the punctuation, spaces and spellings must be the same. Tagging a page with <nowiki>[[Category:Traditional/Folk]] or [[Category:Traditional&Folk]]</nowiki> will not correctly link to [[:Category:Traditional & Folk|Traditional & Folk]] - only <nowiki>[[Category:Traditional & Folk]]</nowiki> will do that. If you are in doubt, you can hit 'edit' on a page that already links to the category you want, copy-paste the formatting, then back out without actually editing the page.

==== Creating Categories & Subcategories ====

If you don't see an existing category that suits your needs, you can create a new category. This is very easy. All you need to do is tag a page with <nowiki>[[Category:Your New Category Here]]</nowiki>, making sure to also link <nowiki>[[:Category:Your New Category Here|Link Text Here]]</nowiki> in the page's text somewhere. It will show up as a red link. When you click that red link, if you are logged in, you will be prompted to create the category page - and MiraHeze MediaWiki will ''automatically'' index all the pages which have been tagged with <nowiki>[[Category:Your New Category Here]]</nowiki> (though it will '''not''' automatically index pages which contain hyperlinks, like <nowiki>[[:Category:Your New Category Here|Category Name]]</nowiki>). 

In many cases, you will be creating a new ''subcategory''. When you are prompted to create the category's page, make sure that you write <nowiki>[[Category:Overarching Category Here]]</nowiki> on the ''category's page'', inserting whatever category it ought to be subcategorised under. For example, if you make a new top-level topic, you should add <nowiki>[[Category:Topics]]</nowiki> into the topic's page, so that it shows up under the index of [[:Category:Topics|Topics]]. If you make a new sub-topic, add the topic's category page; for example, [[:Category:Heraldry|Heraldry]] is a subcategory of [[:Category:SCA (Topic)|SCA (Topic)]], so the [[:Category:Heraldry|Heraldry]] page is tagged with <nowiki>[[Category:SCA (Topic)]]</nowiki>. This automatically makes it not only show up as a subcategory on the [[:Category:SCA (Topic)|SCA (Topic)]] page, but ''also'' show up as a sub-category on the main [[:Category:Topics|Topics]] page - no further work required! 

It is important that categories are all named in the same style, because category names must be exactly right. As said above, <nowiki>[[Category:Traditional/Folk]] or [[Category:Traditional&Folk]]</nowiki> will not correctly link to [[:Category:Traditional & Folk|Traditional & Folk]] - only <nowiki>[[Category:Traditional & Folk]]</nowiki> will do that. Therefore, please name categories in the same style of natural English, capitalising content words. Avoid punctuation other than (), ' and &. A new category for 'Green Eggs and Ham' should be named <nowiki>[[Category:Green Eggs & Ham]]</nowiki>, not GreenEggs&Ham, GreenEggsAndHam, green eggs n ham, Green eggs And Ham, "Green Eggs and Ham", Green Eggs/Ham, or any other variation.

== I want to create a page for a bard ==

First check to see if a page for the bard already exists by looking for them in [[:Category:Bards|Bards]]. They may be listed under another name than the name you are expecting; check their legal name, stage name, SCA persona name, etc. 

If a page does not exist, simply type in the URL https://bardictorch.miraheze.org/wiki/ and then add the name of the bard to the URL. Use underscores instead of spaces. If the page does not exist yet, you should see a "Create" button in the top right. 

Once you have created the page, go to https://bardictorch.miraheze.org/wiki/Template:Bard and copy-paste the content into your new page. You can then fill out the form with all the information you have. Do not actually edit the Template:Bard page!

== I want to create a page for a piece ==

First, check to see if a page for the piece already exists. Look in [[:Category:Pieces|Pieces]] to see if the piece is there, either under the title you know it by or under another title. You may also look at the bard's page to see if it is listed under their works. 

If a page does not exist, simply type in the URL https://bardictorch.miraheze.org/wiki/ and then add the title to the URL. Use underscores instead of spaces. If the page does not exist yet, you should see a "Create" button in the top right. 

For songs:
Once you have created the page, go to [[Template:Song]] and copy-paste the content into your new page. You can then fill out the form with all the information you have. Do not actually edit the Template:Song page!

For period & traditional stories:
As for songs, but use [[Template:Story]]
There is not yet a template for modern, "no shit there I was" stories.

For poems:
As for songs, but use [[Template:Poem]]

For dances with associated music:
As for songs, but use [[Template:Dance & Music]]

For other types of pieces:
We do not yet have a template for other types of pieces. You can help us create one! Fill out the piece page with as much information as you think it should have, and someone else will help improve it later. Make sure you link it into all the categories it should belong to, and link to it from the bard's page, so that others can find the unfinished page.

== I want to help improve existing pages ==

Extremely helpful activities include:
* Finding more performances, and linking to those performances on both the piece's page and the bard's page. When you add a performance to a piece page, if you also link to the bard's page, that's even more helpful. 
* Clicking red links (pages that should exist, but don't yet) and setting up the page. Look at other, similar pages to see how the page should be set up. You can use template pages, too.
* Adding links and categories to pages that ought to be properly interlinked and categorised, but aren't yet. Check whether categories are merely hyperlinked or the page is also properly added to the relevant category, whether categories have sub-categories or should be sorted into overarching sur-categories, and so on. 
* Finding information about licensing, permissions, bards' preferences, etc and linking it on both piece pages and bard pages.

title: Category:Joyful
wikitext:
Joyful should be used for all pieces that are happy, victorious, triumphant (but not [[:Category:Warlike|warlike]]), upbeat, 'party' music or otherwise suitable for celebrations.

Mood tags on Bardic Torch are used to help bards select appropriate works for a particular context. Joyful pieces should be appropriate for performing at parties and celebrations, in taverns, in bardic circles where the mood is upbeat and cheerful, and at other occasions where happy music is called for. 

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]

This is a subcategory of [[:Category:Historical People & Events|Historical People & Events]], for pieces ''about'' the people amd events of the 8th Century. Be careful to distinguish it from [[:Category:8th Century|8th Century]], which is for pieces ''documentable to'' the 8th Century.

When you create new subcategories of [[:Category:Historical People & Events|Historical People & Events]], make sure to tag them with <nowiki>[[Category:Historical People & Events]]</nowiki> so that they show up correctly as subcategories.

[[Category:Historical People & Events]]

title: Category:13th Century
wikitext:
This page is for pieces ''documentable to'' the 13th Century. For pieces ''about'' the events and people of the 13th Century, go to [[:Category:13th Century (Topic)|13th Century (Topic)]]. 

When you create new date-range categories for pieces before the year 1600, make sure to tag them with <nowiki>[[Category:Pre-1600 Sources]]</nowiki> so that they show up correctly as subcategories.

[[Category:Pre-1600 Sources]]

title: Category:Pre-1600 Sources
wikitext:
This category is for pieces that were documentably created, entirely or partially, prior to the year 1600. See [[Categories]] for more information.

Some pieces may be only partially created prior to the year 1600; they may be [[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta]], which set new words to period tunes, or [[:Category:Setting Pieces|Setting Pieces]], which set period words to new tunes.

[[Category:Source Category]]

title: Category:Setting Pieces
wikitext:
This category is for pieces that set historical words to new tunes. Generally, the texts should be from before the year 1600. See also [[:Category:Pre-1600 Sources|Pre-1600 Sources]]. 

If new words are set to a historical tune, the piece belongs in [[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta]]. If new words are set to a tune that is under copyright, the piece belongs in [[:Category:Contrafacta (Modern)|Contrafacta (Modern)]].

See [[Categories]] for more information.

[[Category:Source Category]]

title: Category:Contrafacta
wikitext:
Contrafacta is the source category for pieces that set new words to historical/folk/traditional tunes - also called "parody", "filk", "lyrical adaptation", "rewrite" and so on. 

You may also categorise these pieces as [[:Category:Pre-1600 Sources|Pre-1600 Sources]] (for documentably pre-1600 melodies) or [[:Category:Traditional & Folk|Traditional & Folk]] (for folk tunes), and may categorise them as [[:Category:SCA Pieces|SCA Pieces]] or [[:Category:SF&F Pieces|SF&F Pieces]] if the new words were written by SCA or SF&F-related artists. 

If the piece sets new words to an existing modern tune that is under copyright, use [[:Category:Contrafacta (Modern)|Contrafacta (Modern)]] instead.

If the piece sets existing historical words to a new tune, it belongs in [[:Category:Setting Pieces|Setting Pieces]].

title: Bard Preference Checklist
wikitext:
= Bard Preference Page Checklist =

== What is this page? ==

This checklist aims to be a comprehensive list of everything you might want to include on a bardic preferences page (aka licensing FAQ, etiquette page, permissions page, etc).

=== Why Create a Bard Preference Page? ===

One of the ways that you, as a bard, can really help Bardic Torch is by creating a page that summarises information about your legal rights, licensing, etiquette preferences, performance preferences, and other how-to-interact-with-this-bard's-work instructions. 

We want to make sure that people respect your wishes to the greatest extent possible - and that's easiest to do when people know what they are. That's hard to do when information is scattered across Facebook comments, album liner notes and YouTube descriptions. 

We cannot host unsourced, original information on this wiki. If you create a page that states your wishes, we can link to that page from your profile here so that the information is always available and easy to find.

Creators in the bardic community sometimes have requests that are, outside of the bardic community, relatively unusual; they might, for example, be okay with others performing their work so long as they do it from memory and don't write it down. This means that just using standard licenses like Creative Commons often doesn't capture everything we might want to know about a bard's instructions.

=== How can I use this page? ===

This page is trying to be an exhaustive list of every preference a bard ''might'' have. If you have licensing decisions, preferences, or beliefs around etiquette which you don't see on this page - add them! 

The idea is that you can copy-paste this entire list to your own notes, then delete everything that does not apply to you. Or you can totally rewrite your page from scratch, but use this page as a reference to make sure that you've covered ''everything'' you might want to specify. 

If this is way more detailed than you care for, and you want an easy version, check out the list of [https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/cclicenses/ Creative Commons licenses]. If you state that your work is released under (for example) CC-BY-NC-SA, you'll be using an easy-to-follow guide that many other creators use in the same way. You can also say nothing at all - in which case your work will be protected by the default copyright law in your country.

== The Checklist ==

=== Licensing & Copyright ===

My works are legally... (delete as appropriate)
* all released into the public domain
* released under a Creative Commons license 
** List of Creative Commons licenses: [https://creativecommons.org/licenses/list.en https://creativecommons.org/licenses/list.en]
** List of Creative Commons license codes: [https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/cclicenses/ https://creativecommons.org/share-your-work/cclicenses/]
*** CC BY: it's okay to do anything with the work so long as you credit the creator (give attribution)
*** CC BY-SA: it's okay to do anything with the work so long as you credit the creator (give attribution) and share any adaptations under the same CC BY-SA license 
*** CC BY-NC: it's okay to use the work for noncommercial purposes only, so long as you credit the creator (give attribution)
*** CC BY-NC-SA: it's okay to use the work for noncommercial purposes only, so long as you credit the creator (give attribution) and share your adaptations under the same CC BY-NC-SA license 
*** CC BY-ND: it's okay to copy and distribute the work so long as you don't adapt or change it and you give credit (attribution) to the creator 
*** CC BY-NC-ND: it's okay to copy and distribute the work for noncommercial purposes only, so long as you don't adapt or change it, and you give credit (attribution) to the creator 
* all copyrighted with all rights reserved 
* released under a specific legal license which I will link to 
* released under a variety of different licenses; some might be public domain, while others might be released under Creative Commons, and others might be copyrighted with all rights reserved. Please check the individual work/album page for details. 

If you use a Creative Commons license, you should stick to the terms of the license - don't specify contradictory rules to what the license says.

=== Performance ===

Permission to perform my work is... (delete as appropriate)
* not given; you may not perform my work and shouldn't ask
* available if you ask; you should contact me through (specify contact method) to ask 
** but unlikely to be given unless (specify conditions eg. unless you know me / unless you can offer payment / unless you are using my work strictly noncommercially)
** and likely to be given, so long as you just ask!
** likely to be given, but please perform it to me before you perform it to others so that I can check I'm happy with your rendition 
* available through my label/company/group; to ask, contact (specify contact method)
* given if you belong to a particular group (eg. all SCA bards have permission to perform my work at SCA events / all people who were present at X event have permission to perform my song about X event / all amateur non-professional musicians have permission)
* hereby freely given; if you are reading this, you may perform it

If you perform my work, I: (delete as appropriate)
* must be informed - contact me through (specify contact method) and link to a recording / tell me where and when you performed / tell me how much money you made 
* would love to be informed, but it's not mandatory - it just brings me joy!
* don't need to be informed, but you can tell me if you like 
* actively do not wish to be informed 

=== Adaptations ===

If you want to adapt, remix, build upon, or change my work... (delete as appropriate)
* that's fantastic! I happily encourage this. 
* that's fine - I give permission. 
* that's fine, so long as...
** the adaptation is Fair Use 
** the adaptation is serious - I do not like parodies, or silly or humorous adaptations of serious works 
** the adaptation respects my work - you can localise it or translate it but do not try to 'improve' it
** the changes are minor (eg. move music to a different key or register, change pronouns in a song, cut some parts of a poem to fit a shorter performance slot) and do not fundamentally change the meaning / themes / important cultural aspects of the work 
** you do not change the following aspects which are important to me (specify)
* you should ask me for permission first
** and show me the adaptation before you perform it to others, so I can check I'm happy with it
* that's okay, but only for a live context - don't upload your adaptation to the internet
* please don't - I prefer my work to be shared faithfully, as-is.

If you adapt, change, remix, build upon or change my work, I... (delete as appropriate)
* must be informed - contact me (specify contact method) and show me what you did with my work 
* would love to be informed, but it's not mandatory - it just brings me joy!
* don't need to be informed, but you can tell me if you like 
* actively do not wish to be informed

I am okay with the following kinds of adaptations: (delete as appropriate)
* changing the words to a tune I wrote (aka filk, parody, contrafactum)
* creating fan videos of my songs
* changing the events, plots or characters in my stories
* creating shorter, more concise versions of my pieces without otherwise changing them 
* elaborating on my pieces to create longer works, without otherwise changing them (eg. adding more verses to a song)
* attempts to improve my work or fix perceived issues in my work 
* taking my stories/poems and setting them to music 
* performing your own version of my comedy routine / piece of fooling / jesting / clowning 
* using my songs/poems as part of a musical or stage play 

but I'm not okay with these adaptations: (delete as appropriate)
* changing the words to a tune I wrote (aka filk, parody, contrafactum)
* creating fan videos of my songs
* changing the events, plots or characters in my stories
* creating shorter, more concise versions of my pieces without otherwise changing them 
* elaborating on my pieces to create longer works, without otherwise changing them (eg. adding more verses to a song)
* attempts to improve my work or fix perceived issues in my work 
* taking my stories/poems and setting them to music 
* performing your own version of my comedy routine / piece of fooling / jesting / clowning
* using my songs/poems as part of a musical or stage play

=== Attribution ===

==== Live Performance ====

===== Non-Commercial =====
When you perform my work live in a casual, non-commercial context (eg. around a campfire, at a bardic circle) you should: (delete as appropriate)
* credit my stage name (specify)
* credit my SCA persona name (specify)
* credit my full legal name (specify)
* credit both my SCA/persona/stage name and my full legal name (specify)
* credit whatever name you feel the audience will know me by
* credit my name and an affiliation that is important to me (eg. "name" of "SCA Kingdom", "name" from "musical group")
* you must provide credit if discussing the piece, or if asked who wrote it, but do not need to give it with every performance 
* and state where listeners can find me online (specify a website, blog, search term)
* and state the album/cycle/context that you found the piece in 
* and direct listeners to where they can find my shop/stall/booth at the event, if I'm present at the event/convention/site
* and advertise my performance if I'll be performing later at that event/convention/site
and you should: (delete as appropriate)
* give verbal credit before/after the piece - however seems best to you
* give verbal credit before you begin performing the piece
* give verbal credit after you finish performing the piece
* give verbal credit both before performing and after performing the piece
* give verbal credit, but it's okay if this is once per set or at the beginning or end of the show rather than directly before/after the piece 
* give written credit displayed on a sign, or on a handout/card/flyer
* display a QR code that links to my website (specify)
* use your best judgement to choose a method of attribution that maximises the likelihood that the audience understands it (eg. written formats for loud venues, before a piece if there's lots of noise and applause afterwards, once per show if there's a section for formal credits)
* give credit in whatever format works best for you, so long as attribution is given

* so long as you're an amateur (specify your definition eg. so long as you're not making more than $100/month from music)

=== Recording & Writing ===

When I create a song, poem, or other work, it's: (delete as appropriate)
* not okay to write it down at all - I do not want my work to be recorded at all
* okay to perform it, but not to write it down - I want my work to experience an authentic oral tradition folk process

=== Performance Etiquette ===

Legal Name 058 performing: (delete as appropriate)
* I enthusiastically love it when people sing along, and would enjoy it if you joined in - please do!
* I love people singing along, and I'm also enthusiastic about people harmonising, jamming on instruments, drumming, or joining in however they want to! 
* I am okay with people singing along if they want to - I don't mind either way.
* I don't like people singing along, and would prefer that you didn't
* I don't like people singing along, but I'm okay with people joining in with other kinds of jamming like drumming or humming
* I like it when people sing along, but it throws me off if they harmonise - please only sing along if we're singing the same melody
* I like it when people sing along or jam on instruments, but drumming or clapping along throws me off my rhythmn - please don't drum or clap along
* I love it when people sing along with the chorus and would enjoy it if you joined in, but I don't want anyone to join in with the verses 
* Other (specify!)

In bardic competition: (delete as appropriate)

* I am okay with people competing with my work if I'm not entering the competition, but if I'm entering then please don't perform my work
* I am okay with people competing with my work even if I'm competing alongside them in the competition, but please check with me first to see whether I intended to perform that piece myself. Only compete the piece if it's different to the one I'm performing
* I am okay with people competing with my work so long as they're not on the opposite side of a team-based contest or bardic war point

In bardic circles where I'm present: (delete as appropriate)

* Check with me before performing my work, quietly/privately before the circle begins
* Please check with me before performing my work, but it's okay if that's just a quick question to me when you get up to perform my piece 
* Don't perform my work without permission, but it's okay to approach me for permission if I know you
* Don't perform my work 

When you learn my work for performance: (delete as appropriate)

* Please memorise it and perform it off-book. I do not want people performing my work on-book.
* Please practise it thoroughly before performing - I only want people performing my work with respect and dedication.

=== Objectionable Use ===

I do not want: (delete as appropriate)
* my work to be used for objectionable purposes
* my work to be performed in objectionable contexts 
* my work to be displayed, uploaded, published or performed alongside objectionable content 

When I say "objectionable purposes", I mean: (delete as appropriate)
* religious proselytizing 
* any political content at all
* political content promoting certain parties or beliefs (specify)
* content that promotes hateful groups
* content that is sexist, racist, homophobic, transphobic, anti-immigrant, or promotes prejudice or hatred against anyone based on their sex, gender, race, sexuality, identity, religion or lack of religion, immigration status, disability, neurotype, citizenship, nationality, veteran status, or other characteristics
* illegal or criminal activity 
* advertising for any religious or political group
* advertising for any large corporation
* advertising to sell alcohol, weapons, pornography, or other items (specify)
* anything that involves violence 
* anything that involves graphic violence
* anything that violates my religious beliefs (specify)
* insulting or mocking me
* insulting or mocking anybody else (eg. writing a song parody about a politician)

When I say "objectionable contexts", I mean: (delete as appropriate)
* at any political events, rallies, or protests 
* at political events, rallies, or protests for certain parties or beliefs (specify)
* religious events 
* at events that are for hateful groups
* at events that welcome or include hateful groups
* at events that involve anything that could be considered promotion of violence (eg. martial arts competitions, military recruiting, performances of art that contains graphic violence)
* at events that serve alcohol 
* at adult-themed or sexual events

When I say "objectionable content", I mean: (delete as appropriate)
* any NSFW content
* any content that is inappropriate for children
* profanity
* sexual content of any kind (including non-pornographic sexual content eg. sex education, artistic nudity) 
* pornographic content 
* any content likely to cause problems for corporate relations, advertising, PR, etc 
* content relating to alcohol, cigarettes or other legal drugs
* content relating to illegal drugs (eg. depictions of use)
* content that violates my religious beliefs (specify)
* anything that the average person would find offensive or upsetting

And: (please delete as appropriate)
* If you are not sure whether I would consider something objectionable content, you can contact me to ask.
* I reserve the right to decide that something is objectionable to me and ask you to remove my work or cease performing my work, even if it wasn't in this list.
* I don't mind certain content so long as it is kept private (eg. you can sing parody lyrics about cannabis use in your own camp, but don't upload or publish them) (specify)
* I want to be informed if you see my work in an objectionable context or alongside objectionable content, so that I can send a takedown notice.
* If you see my work performed for objectionable purposes or alongside objectionable content, you have my permission to immediately ask the performer to stop, and let them know that you think I'd object.
* Please don't tell others that you think I'd object to their use of my content - let me make that decision for myself. Ask the performer to contact me.

title: Conservation Status
wikitext:
Conservation status categories exist to help flag works that may need more work to preserve or archive them. 

A work is [[:Category:Low Risk|Low Risk]] if it exists in at least four places. Some examples of places a work might exist:
* Recordings on YouTube 
* Streaming on Spotify 
* Lyrics and sheet music available on the bard's own website/blog
* Lyrics and sheet music (or performance videos) archived on a community/SCA archive such as MidBards or CalonSong
* Lyrics and sheet music exist in hard copy, stored in a known archive or library (with contact details available)
* A story or poem exists in a book, archived in a known library or storage (with contact details available)
* A story or poem exists in a book, available to purchase from a known vendor
* Album or CD is available to purchase from a known vendor 
* The author can be contacted to ask for a copy, with known/public contact details
* The work is securely established in the oral tradition, with a large number of bards keeping it memorised

A work is [[:Category:Endangered|Endangered]] if it exists in less than three known places, and it is not [[:Category:Restricted|Restricted]].

A work is [[:Category:Critically Endangered|Critically Endangered]] if contributors to the wiki are unable to find the work, or only partially able to find the work (eg. the lyrics of a song are available, but the melody is not) and it is not [[:Category:Restricted|Restricted]]. References to it may exist in indexes or history texts, but the work itself may not be easily available for download/purchase/request anywhere.

A work is [[:Category:Restricted|Restricted]] if the creator does not allow the work to be recorded, archived, or shared. These works should not be categorised as [[:Category:Endangered|Endangered]] or [[:Category:Critically Endangered|Critically Endangered]], because those categories exist to help flag works which need more effort to preserve or find them, and these works should not be preserved or found. 

You can help the archive by: 
* If you know of performances, lyrics, recordings, or places to purchase or acquire works that are Endangered or Critically Endangered, please add links to the piece's page
* If you notice that a page in the Endangered category has acquired sufficient links to move into the Low Risk category, please move it there
* If you notice that a page in the Critically Endangered category has acquired sufficient links to move into the Endangered category, please move it there
* If you have a copy of a piece that is Endangered or Critically Endangered, please consider hosting it on your own site elsewhere so that we can link to it from the wiki
* If you notice that a work in the Low Risk category is now Endangered, because it is no longer archived (eg. the websites hosting the piece have gone down, the piece has been removed from the websites that hosted it, the person who archived the hard copy of the piece can no longer be contacted, the seller is no longer selling the piece), please move it to the Endangered or Critically Endangered category

title: Category:Comedic
wikitext:
The wiki uses a limited number of mood tags to help ensure work is findable and the tag system remains manageable. The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag.

Comedic should be used for pieces that are comic, humorous, silly, parodies, lighthearted or otherwise suitable for the lightening of moods (and unsuitable for serious occasions).

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].

== Lyrics ==
There are several versions of this song. In every version, the main character becomes a knight and dies in battle. In some, the last chorus forms their final words, with some versions cutting off at "I have lived by my oath -" and others finishing the line, "I have lived by my oath, now I die." In other versions, an additional verse is sung to celebrate the knight's legacy, call their heirs to arms, or encourage squires to live up to the example. The knight's gender varies.
* [https://www.deviantart.com/arrowdel/art/I-was-born-on-the-Listfield-384327041 Lyrics on DeviantArt, with one version of the final verse]
* [https://www.beadmaker.se/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/p%C3%A4rlmakerskans-engelska-version-3.0.pdf Lyrics in the Beadmaker's Songbook, with a female main character and the 'now I die' ending]

----
== Licensing & Etiquette ==
According to SCA oral tradition, Ivar Battleskald initially forbade his songs from being written down, wanting them to be passed on only via oral tradition. He wished to experiment with seeing how the songs would grow and change as they spread through the SCA. Later in his life he permitted his songs to be written down, only asking that they never be sung from paper - only sung from memory. 
* [https://bardic.avacal.net/SongBook/SP01.html Discussion on the Avacal Bardic page]

This song is known by any number of alternative names, including:
* The Barbarian Birthday Dirge / The Barbarian Birthday Song
* The Viking Birthday Dirge / The Viking Birthday Song
* The Vulgar Birthday Song
* The Mongolian Birthday Song
* The SCA Birthday Song / The SCA Happy Birthday
* HAPPY BIRTHDAY (THUD)

== Key Links ==
The song is sung to a simplified version of the melody of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Song_of_the_Volga_Boatmen Song of the Volga Boatmen / Эй, ухнем!]. You can listen to [https://youtu.be/xNVPw5ReQHE a recording of this Russian song on YouTube].

----
== Lyrics ==
There are numerous verses and numerous versions of the verses; the number of verses sung will depend on the occasion and on the tolerance of the birthday celebrant.
After each 'happy birthday', it is traditional to either make a loud thud by dropping something heavy, stomp your feet, or literally say the word 'thud'.
