title: FAQ for Bards
wikitext:
= FAQ for Bards =

== Your Page ==

=== Why do I have a page at Bardic Torch? ===

Bardic Torch aims to record information about as many bards & bardic works as possible, and ensure that the information is archived so that works aren't lost/forgotten. We aim to create a page for ''every'' bard whose work is worth preserving. If someone likes your work, they probably made you a page. 

=== What if I don't want to have a page at Bardic Torch? ===

State somewhere public - on a personal website, blog, or other page that we can cite - that you don't want people to archive your works / don't want to have wiki pages created about you / don't want any information about you to be online / etc. Send us a link. If you do not have or want an account here, you can [https://forms.gle/wUwWnMKtWZSUisWCA contact us via Google Form].

We will edit your page (or you can edit it yourself) to be a blank page that just says, "This bard prefers not to have a wiki page. Citation: (link)". 

Please make sure that the link is to a public page (so we can all access it), a permanent page (so the citation doesn't disappear when the page goes away), and a page where you are identifiable (so we know that the actual bard requested this, and it isn't some random other saboteur or mischief-maker).

We do it this way because this is a publicly editable wiki that anyone can edit. If we simply deleted or took down your page, it would be possible for someone else to inadvertently put it back up in the future, not realising that you'd asked to take it down. Even if we prevented anyone else from making a new page, someone else might add you to other bardic indexes/archives/songbooks in the future. By having your page state that you do not wish to have a wiki page, we can ensure everybody in the future knows how to respect your wishes. 

For other things you might want to post publicly, see the [[Bard Preference Checklist]]. 

=== Can I edit my own page? ===

Absolutely - please do. We'd love to have contributions from bards; you know more about your work than anyone else! 

See [[Get Started Contributing]] for more.

== Your Rights ==

=== Is Bardic Torch violating my copyright? ===

We really hope not! We have a strict policy against putting copyrighted information on the wiki. In fact, we try not to host works directly on the wiki at all. We only link to where you can find works elsewhere. 

People are not allowed to upload audio or video to Bardic Torch. If you find that someone is doing so, please feel free to remove the content (Bardic Torch is a publicly editable wiki, editable by anyone) or let us know. If you don't have or want an account here, you can do this [https://forms.gle/wUwWnMKtWZSUisWCA via Google Form]. 

People are allowed to post lyrics to Bardic Torch, but only if the page can cite a source that shows the author has agreed for their lyrics to be shared and re-published anywhere.

It is possible that you find links on Bardic Torch to pages that are violating your copyright - eg. songbooks that host your lyrics under the wrong license, YouTube channels uploading performances of your songs without permission, or other performers performing your work without crediting you. We are not responsible for content on other websites; you will need to contact the host of the songbook / complain to YouTube / ask the performer to stop. All we can do is remove the link; the content will still be online. 

=== I have rules about how people use my work. How can I share these? ===

State somewhere public - on a personal website, blog, or other page that we can cite - that you have rules about how people use your work, and explain what they are. Edit your page to include a link to your statement (or [https://forms.gle/wUwWnMKtWZSUisWCA send us the link], if you're not sure how to edt your own page). We will try to include your rules both on your own bard page and on any relevant piece pages. 

Please make sure that the link is to a public page (so we can all access it), a permanent page (so the citation doesn't disappear when the page goes away), and a page where you are identifiable (so we know that the actual bard requested this, and it isn't some random other saboteur or mischief-maker).

We do it this way because this is a publicly editable wiki that anyone can edit. If you simply edit your page to say "I don't like my songs to be written down without permission" or "I'm okay with others performing my work so long as it's not-for-profit" then we have no source for that information - and no idea if it was really you who wrote it. We cannot risk hosting false information about copyright; if someone who ''isn't'' the author writes "everyone has permission to perform this song", and the real author doesn't want the song to be performed by anyone except themselves, that could lead to a lot of copyright violations. By linking to a source for the information, we can make sure that future editors know that the author of the work genuinely made those statements about licensing/sharing/etiquette/etc.

See the [[Bard Preference Checklist]] for help figuring out what you might want to publish.

== Your Works == 

=== Can I edit my own song/story/poem pages? ===

Yes! We love when bards help expand our wiki; you know more about your work than anyone else. Please see [[Get Started Contributing]]. 

=== Can I upload my work to Bardic Torch? ===

'''No.''' Do not upload your work directly to Bardic Torch. We cannot host it. 

We are a publicly editable wiki that anyone can edit. We cannot risk hosting content directly; it would be very easy for someone to (inadvertently or deliberately) upload copyrighted content. 

You can upload your work to:
* YouTube
* Your own personal website or blog 
* Spotify, BandCamp, SoundCloud or other music-sharing services 
* Several SCA indexes, eg. MidBards; see [[Collections]]
* All of the above simultaneously! 

You can then link, from your pieces' pages, to any and all of those sources. 

The only exception is if you have made it publicly clear, in a way that is attributable to you as the author, that your work is okay for anyone to republish and share freely. We need a citation for this. If you upload your song to your blog and state "I give permission for anyone to share the lyrics to this song or republish them in their own songbooks", or upload a song to a music sharing service and license it as Creative Commons BY-SA, then we can also share the lyrics on Bardic Torch, citing your blog post as evidence that the author has given permission.

title: Category:Contrafacta (Modern)
wikitext:
This category is for pieces which put new words to the tune of an existing song where the copyright for the song belongs to somebody else. '''The legal situation for recording or performing such songs can be fraught.'''

See [[Categories]] for more information about how works are categorised on Bardic Torch. See [[:Category:Contrafacta|Contrafacta]] for pieces where the tune is historical/folk/traditional. 

Contrafacta (singular contrafactum) are also known as parodies, filk, adaptations and rewrites. We use the term contrafacta at BardicTorch because it is clear and unambiguous, whereas 'filk' is sometimes used to refer to all SF&F music or the entire 'nerd folk' community.

title: Category:Borrowings
wikitext:
Use this category for modern pieces that are often 'borrowed' into the bardic tradition, despite being created by modern authors who may not be associated with the bardic community. This includes professional folk singers who are not publicly involved with SCA/fandom/LARP/convention/filk culture.

'''Recording & performance of these works can be fraught, because they are usually under copyright, and performers/creators/musicians outside the bardic community often have less permissive views about community members using their work'''.

title: Category:Moods
wikitext:
The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag. 

Try to use one of the broad categories listed in [[Categories]] as a piece's mood in its infobox.

It is possible to create more specific categories, which should be listed here by tagging the category page with <nowiki>[[Category:Moods]]</nowiki>, but remember that the 'mood' tag is intended to help bards find pieces appropriate for a particular '''context or situation'''. We do not intend to split the 'Joyful' tag into 'Excited', 'Happy', 'Cheerful' or other extremely subjective sub-categories. You might, however, create a new category under 'Warlike' for songs suitable as marching songs, or a new category under 'Tragic' for songs specifically suitable at funerals/rememberances, or a new category under 'Romantic' for songs appropriate at weddings.

[[Category:Top Level Categories]]

title: Category:Opening Songs
wikitext:
Use this category for songs that are considered traditional 'opening songs' with which to begin a concert or open up a bardic circle. 

Songs in this category should either be ''widespread and traditional'' opening songs, or should specifically have themes/lyrics regarding welcoming bards, saying hello and welcome, or opening up a new performance space; do not add songs that are purely one group's idiosyncratic tradition. 

See also [[:Category:Leaving Songs|Leaving Songs]].

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]

title: Category:Relaxed
wikitext:
Relaxed should be used for songs that are chill, calming, peaceful, soothing, lullabies or otherwise suitable for a late-night quiet campfire with a sleepy audience. 

Mood tags on Bardic Torch are used to help bards select appropriate works for a particular context. Relaxed pieces should be suitable for contexts where bards need to be quiet because people are sleeping, or need to be more relaxed to help calm children down before bedtime, or in situations where people are too stressed to enjoy loud/fast/passionate music.

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]

title: Category:Dance Music
wikitext:
The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag. 

Dance music should be music that people want to dance to. This might include historical music that has a specific dance associated, or might simply be upbeat music with a strong even beat that people frequently enjoy dancing to.

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]

title: Category:Story (Mood)
wikitext:
This mood tag is used for pieces that are too complex to categorise into a single [[Category:Moods|Mood]] tag, because they contain a plot.

For example, a song where a young squire strives to become a knight might be [[:Category:Warlike|Warlike]], a song where the squire celebrates becoming knighted might be [[:Category:Joyful|Joyful]], and a song where the knight dies might be [[:Category:Tragic|Tragic]]. If a song follows the entire journey from the young squire's first battle to the old knight's eventual death, it should not be categorised with all three moods; instead, it belongs here.

The intent of a 'mood' tag is to help bards find repertoire that will work in a particular context: a performer at a party or a bar may be seeking happy or funny pieces and wishing to avoid tragic pieces, while a performer at a funeral may have the opposite preference. A song's mood does not have to be perfectly captured by the tag, so long as it would be appropriate to perform in similar contexts to the other songs in the tag. 

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]

title: Category:Story Mood
wikitext: #REDIRECT [[:Category:Story (Mood)]]

title: Category:Romantic
wikitext:
Romantic should be used for music that may be suitable for romantic occasions. For example, it might be pieces suitable weddings, or flirtatious pieces that a bard might perform to a romantic interest while flirting with them, or it may include praise pieces about the performer's partner/spouse/inspiration.

Mood tags on Bardic Torch are used to help bards select appropriate works for a particular context. Not all pieces on the [[:Category:Topics|topic]] of [[:Category:Love|Love]] will be suitable for the Romantic mood tag.

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]

title: Category:Eerie
wikitext:
Mood tags on Bardic Torch are used to help bards select appropriate works for a particular context. Eerie pieces do not necessarily have to be on supernatural or horrifying [[:Category:Topics|topics]]. Categorise as 'Eerie' songs that are scary, eerie, creepy, sinister, ghostly, chilling, fear-inducing or unsettling; suitable for Halloween celebrations, spooky song contests, or to perform alongside ghost stories.

See all [[:Category:Moods|Moods]] or read more at [[Categories]].
[[Category:Moods]]

title: Easy Start Add a Song
wikitext:
= Easy Start: Add A Song =

== Step 1: Create an account ==
Miraheze sometimes blocks new users from creating new pages, especially pages with external links, if they don't have a confirmed email address or a history of editing pages before creating new ones. We are actively working to get the permissions set up in a better way for our wiki. For now, if you have any trouble creating a page, you may need to follow the troubleshooting checklist:

* Confirm your email address. (You may need to check your spam folder.)
* Try editing a page before creating a new one.
* Try creating a page without any external links. You can then edit the page to add in the links. 
* If all of this fails, contact the administrator. Forannán Glórach (Atlantia) is the current maintainer of the wiki. You can also use this [https://forms.gle/wUwWnMKtWZSUisWCA contact form]. 

== Step 2: Check to see if the song page already exists ==

All pieces should show up in [[:Category:Pieces]]. You can use a ctrl+F search there, the main search bar at the top of the wiki page, or [[Special:Search]] to search for the song's title. 

Try searching for the elements in the title which are shared between multiple versions. (For example, if a piece is sometimes known as "The Daring Exploits of Knight McKnight", sometimes as "Daring Exploits of Knight McKnight" and sometimes simply as "Knight McKnight", try searching just for "Knight McKnight". That way, it should show up even if the page isn't named what you expect.) If you know a song by a different title, you don't have to create a separate page for it; you could create a redirect, so that anyone who searches for "The Daring Exploits of Knight McKnight" is simply redirected to the existing page for "Knight McKnight". However, creating redirects isn't covered in this guide. 

If you're not sure what the title might be, you can also search [[:Category:Bards]] for the author (or use the search bar at the top of the site to look for the author). It may be listed on their bard/author page. 

If the song doesn't already have a page, congrats! You've found a piece that will be very useful to contribute to our wiki!

== Step 3: Find the 'create page' button. ==

The easiest way to create a page is to follow a red link. Red links go to pages that don't exist yet. 

For example, if the song "The Daring Exploits of Knight McKnight" is a song by Legal Name 122, you can edit Legal Name 122's bard page so that the song is listed under their works. The easiest way to create an internal link is to surround it with double square brackets: <nowiki> [[The Daring Exploits of Knight McKnight]]</nowiki> 

Once you save your edit to the bard's page, you should see a red link show up like: [[The Daring Exploits of Knight McKnight]]. When you click on it, you'll be taken to a page that says it doesn't exist, and asks you if you'd like to create the page. 

If you just want to add a song, and don't want to deal with editing other pages (or the bard's page doesn't exist yet), then you can simply go to the URL bar at the top of your browser. On this page, it should display "https://bardictorch.miraheze.org/wiki/Easy_Start_Add_a_Song". Simply type in the URL for the song you want to create. For example, you can type in "https://bardictorch.miraheze.org/wiki/The_Daring_Exploits_of_Knight_McKnight" and hit enter. Remember to use underscores instead of spaces. This method should also take you to a page that prompts you as to whether you'd like to create a page. 

If using the template is too complex or difficult, it is absolutely fine to simply create the page, add the information you know, and leave it for somebody else to update it with the template later. Simply add what you want to add, then ensure you write <nowiki>[[Category:Songs]] [[Category:Pieces]]</nowiki> at the bottom of the page. This will categorise it in the list of songs and pieces, so that another user can find it later and improve the page.

== Step 4: Copy-paste the template. ==

This guide will walk you through using [[Template:BlankSong]]. Go there now and simply copy-paste the text you see on the page (you don't need to edit the template). 

The template with hints in is at [[Template:Song]] and should be suitable for most users. If it's a little intimidating or you just want to use a blank template, stick to [[Template:BlankSong]]. 

Copy-paste the text of the template into the page that you are creating. 

== Step 5: Fill in the title. ==

At the top of the template, it should say TITLE, surrounded by equals signs. Do not touch the equals signs - they are the formatting that makes the title display as a title. Simply write the title of the song in the place where it says TITLE. 

In the infobox, you will also see:

<nowiki>| title = </nowiki>

Simply write the title again in this field, eg: <nowiki>| title = Daring Exploits</nowiki>. This second field can be a great place to add additional alternate titles and nicknames that the song might be known by. 

== Step 6: Save the page. ==

At this point, you have '''already done something useful'''. If you save the page now, it will add the page to the list of [[:Category:Pieces]] and also to the list of [[:Category:Songs]]. Even if you do nothing else, that's helpful! Other editors can come along later and see that information needs to be added to the song's page. Telling us that a song exists by this name tells us where to search, and using the blank template makes it easy for other editors to add information later.

Saving the page now will help make sure that your work isn't lost if you have an issue later. 

== Step 7: Add the author information. ==

In the infobox, you will see two fields: 

<poem>
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
</poem>

Fill those out with the name(s) of the authors. It is very helpful if you can surround the names of the authors with square brackets. For example: 

<poem>
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
scrubbedlyric placeholder line
</poem>

This will create links to the bards' pages. If the bard's pages don't exist yet, they will be red links for now, and someone can click on them if they want to create the bard's page. If/when somebody creates a page for those bards, the red links will ''automatically'' turn into links to the bard's page - no editing required! 

If the bard already has a page on the wiki, please try to use the same name as their page uses. For example, if Legal Name 122's real name is Legal Name 123, but she publishes her work under her SCA Legal Name 054 McBard, use "Legal Name 122" so that the links direct users to her bard page. If the bard does not have a page, try to use the name that they most often publish/share their work under. 

== Step 8: Add categories. ==

Categories are what allow users to search pieces on Bardic Torch for pieces that they want to perform. Try to add as many as you can, but don't worry if you don't know how to use all of them. It is totally okay to leave some fields blank. Another editor can add the information later. You only have to contribute what you know and are comfortable contributing. 

We will use 'mood' as an example, but the same procedure can apply to any of the tags. 

The "mood" field helps categorise songs that are appropriate for different settings - happy songs for singing at parties, sad songs for singing at funerals, sentimental songs for singing at a ceremony, and so on. See [[:Category:Moods]] and select a mood category that seems to fit the piece. In the infobox - where it says <nowiki>| mood = </nowiki> - write the category in the format: <nowiki>[[:Category:TagHere|TagHere]]</nowiki>. For example, <nowiki>| mood = [[:Category:Comedic|Comedic]]</nowiki>. 

The square brackets tells the wiki to create an internal link to another page on the wiki. Using the : before Category tells the wiki to make it a clickable link in the infobox, rather than adding the category to the bottom of the page. Everything before the | tells the wiki what page to link to. Everything after the | tells the wiki what to display as the link text. 

Once you add a category tag, please '''also''' go to the bottom of the page and add the same tag, but in the format <nowiki>[[Category:TagHere]]</nowiki> - eg. <nowiki>[[Category:Comedic]]</nowiki>. This doesn't create a clickable link, the way that the format in the infobox does. Instead, it tells the wiki to actually add the page to the category. This is what makes the page show up in the list - so that when a user goes to [[:Category:Comedic]] your page will automatically be included in the alphabetized list of comedic songs. 

You can use the same procedure for adding a topic (see [[:Category:Topics]]), a culture (see [[:Category:Cultures]]) and a source category (see [[:Category:Source Category]]. You can add multiple topics or multiple categories.

[[Categories]] has more information.

== Step 9: Save again. ==

This will help make sure that your important categorising work isn't lost if you have any difficulty with adding external links.

== Step 10: Add links to external pages. ==

=== Key Links ===

"Key Links" exists to help highlight links that are especially important to a song. For example, if the author themselves has published the song on their own blog, or the author has an official page where you can buy the album, that is the 'canonical' link to the song. Users might want to be able to find it more easily than they find third-party lyrics pages or third-party performances. 

It's okay to leave this blank if you don't have any key links for this song.

If you do have a key link to add, then under Key Links, hit enter twice and then use an asterisk (*) to create a bullet point.

=== Licensing & Etiquette ===

This is where you can add any information like "the bard says it is okay for anyone to perform this song so long as it's for free" or "the bard requests that this song is never written down and only shared through oral tradition" or "the bard released this song into the public domain" or "the bard asks that you get her permission before performing this song, if she's at the event". You should link to the webpage, blog post, social media post, video, etc where the bard shared this information. 

'''Important: You must have a citation for this information, even if you are the bard.''' We cannot verify that you are the bard from your Bardic Torch account. ''Anyone'' could edit a page to say "the bard is okay with people selling her work" - and we can't risk someone adding that kind of information erroneously or maliciously, as it would make us responsible for copyright violations. Please post this information from your personal account or on your personal webpage, and then '''cite''' that page when you add information to the wiki. 

=== Performances & Recordings ===

You cannot add performances or recordings directly to the wiki; you must link to resources elsewhere. If you can't find a performance or recording online, it's totally fine to leave this blank. 

If you do have a link to add, then under Performances & Recordings, hit enter twice and then use an asterisk (*) to create a bullet point. 

To add an external link, use single square brackets, and put the text of the link after the URL. For example, <nowiki>[https://bardictorch.miraheze.org/ The wiki is here!]</nowiki> creates a link that looks like: [https://bardictorch.miraheze.org/ The wiki is here!]

In the text after the link, please include as much information as you can about the performance/recording. Who is performing the piece? Where? When? Who uploaded it to the internet? What website are you linking to? For example: "Performance on YouTube, uploaded by So-and-so, of the song performed by Such-and-such at Event Name in 2026". This will really help people find the piece again if, in the future, links go dead or websites go down. 

If this is too complicated, it's okay to just copy-paste the URL.
